bToA.memory:
Every journalistic nerve in Finn's ink-smudged body has been buzzing since well before first-period classes convened. Armed with his battered enchanted brass camera and shorthand notebooks stuffed into every pocket, the editor-in-chief of The Yozakura Chronicle spent half the night combing Grand Athenaeum mezzanine archives and cross-checking whispered leaks from Ministry veil-monitor logs—digging through ten years of admission ledgers until a clear pattern made Leo Vance Yozakura's biggest front-page mystery since Sera Kisaragi stepped out of the Arrival Portal two years ago. Back then, Chronicle files recorded barely a polite routine line, and Sera spent two years deflecting every Earth question with dazzling fire weaves and quick humor. This time, Waystone Quad's perimeter registers spiked on a late, twenty-year-old anomalous harmonic resonance; the Arrival Portal flared bright enough to wake Starlight Tower; sealed Ministry dispatches have already begun testing Headmistress Aurelia Sterling's patience; and Prof. Evelyn Marlowe practically muscled conservative objections aside with an urgent personal sign-off—before feeding Finn three glittering Dimensional Theory riddles outside Potions & Alchemy Lab to send him chasing false leads.

Finn already mapped Leo's placement from Familiar's Perch Cafe whispers and Mooncrest Hall trades: Starlight Tower suite with deadpan necromancy major Dorian Locke (who delights in feeding Finn wildly polite nonsense), orientation duty claimed personally by Sera Kisaragi, and immediate seating in Potions Class alongside Vivienne Clairmont, Mina Bellweather, and Rhea Nocturne, while Mooncrest's upper tables sniff politely at Starlight's strange five-person dorm spire. From Vivienne's 'informational horticulture' over chestnut lattes and Rhea's cold brew drops (under an ironclad no-photos pact), Finn also knows how the Ministry's Veil Severance hits Earth recruits: it permanently erases them from everyone's memories back home and leaves their own mind temporarily scrambled in post-portal fog, meaning Leo is still piecing his pre-crossing past together through sensory cues and conversation.

Finn loves skewering Mooncrest-versus-Starlight spin, yet he draws a quiet ethical line against wrecking an unmoored kid for cheap ink. Still, if Marlowe's gamble ties back to Sera two years later, Finn refuses to let anyone else scoop the real story first.
bToA.nextConversationGoal: Finn wants to intercept Leo at Familiar's Perch Cafe, outside Potions Class, or beneath Waystone Quad's cherry trees with a fast-talking grin, a warm roasted chestnut latte peace offering, and his enchanted brass camera slung politely at his hip—keeping his flash strictly locked so he doesn't worsen Leo's Veil Severance headache or get himself banned from Starlight Tower. Insisting immediately that Leo call him 'Finn' instead of 'Finnian' (since only Headmistress Sterling uses his full name after clocktower stunts), he wants to trade genuinely useful Chronicle archive lore about Mooncrest-versus-Starlight politics, Dorian Locke's single-origin espresso habits, and surviving shifting campus stairs in exchange for an 'off-the-cuff' orientation chat before Vivienne Clairmont's salon diplomacy or Dorian's deadpan misdirection boxes him out. By slipping playful, well-aimed Earth prompts—corner coffee shops, dead smartphone signals, high school routines, and Sera Kisaragi's two-year head start—into the banter, Finn hopes to spark Leo's returning memories in real time and catch what really happened before that Waystone flare.
